title: ‘Peaky Blinders’ Helps U.K. Region Land Official Production Hub Status From British Film Commission
description: “Peaky Blinders” may have given closely clipped back and sides haircuts a new lease of life, but it’s now helped a region of the U.K. land official
body:
“Peaky Blinders” may have given closely clipped back and sides haircuts a new lease of life, but it’s now helped a region of the U.K. land official backing as a center for high-end productions. 

	The British Film Commission has announced that the West Midlands, home to the city of Birmingham and where “Peaky Blinders” is set and shot, has been named the U.K.’s eighth official regional production hub for scripted inward investment for film and high-end TV. 
	

	According to the Commission, having served as production base for “Peaky Blinders,” the feature film “The Immortal Man” and the as-yet untitled “Peaky Blinders” spin-off series, the region has now fulfilled the criteria needed to receive official hub status. 


	The West Midlands joins South-West England (Bristol); North-West England (Manchester and Liverpool); Yorkshire (Leeds); Northern Ireland (Belfast); Scotland (Glasgow and Edinburgh); Wales (Cardiff); and London & South-East England as an official production hub, lending its strength to a UK-wide offer which contributed £5.8 billion ($7.8 billion) to the UK economy in 2025. 

	“As Tommy Shelby of the Peaky Blinders once said, ‘when you plan something well, there’s no need to rush.’ The growing success of the West Midlands as a U.K. production hub certainly bears this out. Over the course of nearly 15 years, the region has steadily grown in strength and stature, building skills, infrastructure and reputation,” said Adrian Wootton, Chief Executive of the British Film Commission.

	“With the West Midlands becoming an official regional production hub, our offer to the global film and TV industry now spans the length and breadth of the U.K.: wherever you base your production, you’re within a stone’s throw of world-class facilities, crew and talent, with access to one-of-a-kind locations and some of the world’s most stable, transparent and generous tax incentives.”
	

	The two upcoming “Peaky Blinders” spin-off series are being film at the recently opened in Birmingham’s Digbeth Loc. Studios, which was founded by show creator Steven Knight. 

	“I’m thrilled that the West Midlands has been recognised as a fantastic place to make film and TV,” said Knight. The opening of Digbeth Loc. Studios is an important part of that ambition, providing a home for world-class film and television production in the heart of Birmingham. We are at the beginning of a journey, and we’ve got off to a great start. The West Midlands is always ambitious, and we believe we will create a global content making industry in our neighbourhood.”

	In addition to the region’s new hub status, the BBC previously announced plans to establish its future regional headquarters in The Tea Factory in Digbeth .

schema.headline: ‘Peaky Blinders’ Helps U.K. Region Land Official Production Hub Status From British Film Commission

title: CNN Appoints Stefano Pozzebon as Rome Correspondent, Boosting European Coverage (EXCLUSIVE)
description: CNN has announced the appointment of award-winning Italian journalist Stefano Pozzebon as an international correspondent based in its Rome bureau.
body:
CNN has announced the appointment of award-winning Italian journalist Stefano Pozzebon as an international correspondent based in its Rome bureau.

	Pozzebon will be responsible for covering major news stories in Italy and across Europe for CNN’s linear and digital platforms. He will work alongside CNN Vatican Correspondent Christopher Lamb, who leads CNN’s coverage of the Vatican and the papacy of Pope Leo.


	 Pozzebon, who studied International Journalism at City University, London, is fluent in English, Spanish and Portuguese as well as his native Italian. He previously served as a contributor for CNN in Bogota, Colombia, and before that in Caracas, Venezuela, where he was instrumental in the network’s coverage across Latin America in English and Spanish. 
	

	Pozzebon “most recently reported from Venezuela after twin earthquakes struck the country within seconds of each other, causing widespread damage and killing thousands of people,” according to a CNN statement. He also reported on Colombia’s recent presidential election and the ongoing changes inside Venezuela “since U.S. forces snatched Venezuelan strongman Nicolas Maduro earlier this year,” it went on to note.

	Pozzebon, who is 35, was named to the Forbes 30 Under 30 Italy list in 2017 and also nominated for a 2016 Livingston Award for a documentary about fake pharmaceutical trafficking in Western Africa.

	“CNN is committed to investing in on-the-ground reporting in Europe, which continues to play a pivotal role in many of the biggest stories shaping the global agenda – from politics and the environment to sport, culture and more,” Andrew Roy, CNN London Bureau Chief and EMEA General Manager, said in the statement.
	

	He added: “Stefano is an experienced, multilingual journalist with deep roots in the region, making him uniquely placed to deliver authoritative, original reporting that will help audiences understand what’s happening across Europe and the Mediterranean, and why it matters to the rest of the world.”

schema.headline: CNN Appoints Stefano Pozzebon as Rome Correspondent, Boosting European Coverage (EXCLUSIVE)

title: MS NOW Launches Peter Alexander’s ‘State of Play’ August 10
description:
Peter Alexander carries his years of experience at NBC News over to MS NOW, where he lands next week.

	The veteran Washington correspondent and wee
body:
Peter Alexander carries his years of experience at NBC News over to MS NOW, where he lands next week.

	The veteran Washington correspondent and weekend “Today” host will launch a new 11 a.m. program on the Versant-backed network starting Monday, August 10. “State of Play” is billed as focusing on “authoritative and original reporting, thoughtful conversations, and in-depth analysis of the biggest political and national stories shaping the day,” according to a memo from Greg Kordick, the network’s senior vice president of programming.
	

	Alexander left his post at NBC News in March. In his new role at MS NOW, he will also serve as a breaking-news anchor and national correspondent, and contribute to some of the sports coverage broadcast by Versant’s other properties, which include Golf Channel and the USA cable network.


	“The launch of ‘State of Play’ strengthens our programming at a pivotal moment in the country and further positions MS NOW at the center of the 2028 election cycle,” Kordick said. “With the midterm elections quickly approaching and the race for the White House beginning to take shape the day after, we are well-positioned to play a leading role in covering the stories, issues, and campaigns that will define the years ahead.”

	MS NOW recently overhauled its daytime schedule, leaving an hour open in anticipation of Alexander’s expected arrival.  The network has a long history of offering a one-hour program tied to events in Washington, D.C. Andrea Mitchell hosted such a show for nearly two decades when the network was called MSNBC. Alexander will follow Stephanie Ruhle and then hand off to Alicia Menendez and, later, Katy Tur. 
	

	Alexander logged 15 years on the White House beat and worked “Today” weekends since 2018. During that time, he has gained notice for asking reasonable questions of President Trump that for some reason spark blowback. During 2020’s coronavirus pandemic, for example, Alexander asked Trump, then in his first term in the Oval Office, “What do you say to Americans who are watching you right now who are scared?” Trump lashed out. “I say that you’re a terrible reporter!” he retorted.

	Alexander initially joined NBC News in 2004, covering a range of stories around the globe and in the U.S. He was assigned to cover the Republican presidential race in 2012 before being named a White House correspondent that year. He served a stint as a national correspondent between 2014 and 2016, and then was named co-chief White House correspondent alongside Kristen Welker. He kept those duties when he was named co-anchor of Saturday “Today” and became the network’s sole chief White House correspondent when Welker was elevated to moderator of “Meet the Press.”

schema.headline: MS NOW Launches Peter Alexander’s ‘State of Play’ August 10

title: CBS News Correspondent Trevor Phillips Says Editor-in-Chief Bari Weiss ‘Will Either Change the World or Crash and Burn’
description:
Recently appointed CBS News correspondent Trevor Phillips has given a typically forthright assessment of his new boss, Bari Weiss.

	“Bari and her t
body:
Recently appointed CBS News correspondent Trevor Phillips has given a typically forthright assessment of his new boss, Bari Weiss.

	“Bari and her team have a huge tanker of a network news organisation to turn around, and they are assembling a little team on the bridge,” he told The Daily Telegraph. “The great thing about her is that she’s one of those people who will either change the world or crash and burn. But when they crash and burn, it’s in technicolour.”
	

	Phillips, who has been a correspondent for the U.K.’s Sky News since 2021, was handpicked by CBS News editor-in-chief Weiss to join the Paramount-owned network as senior global affairs correspondent. He will also join “60 Minutes.” A veteran writer and broadcaster as well as a former politician, Phillips was previously chair of the U.K.’s Equality and Human Rights Commission and in 2022 was knighted for his services to equality and human rights .


	He is set to move across the pond this summer to take up the new role at CBS. “You know, I’m 72. It’s a great adventure,” he said of Weiss’s offer. “And who turns down adventures if someone is willing to take a chance on you?”

	To mark the move, Phillips gave a wide-ranging interview to the Telegraph, in which he gamely discussed some of the controversy that has swirled since Weiss was appointed to her role last year. “In the U.S., the controversy has been framed as, ‘CBS News is becoming anti-woke’. But that’s not what Bari is about,” Phillip said. “She has her own views, some of which I’m sympathetic to, some of which I’m not, but her point is that the media should be heterodox. There should be a variety of voices.”
	

	He wouldn’t comment on rumors that reporter Holly Williams, who works in CBS News’ London bureau, had been taken off an interview with right wing politician Nigel Farage in favor of Phillips, but said: “What’s interesting in politics now is this current of thought, represented by Farage, Giorgia Meloni and Marine Le Pen, which essentially says the way we have done conventional politics is bust in a new world, and we need to do things differently. We keep trying to fit it into the old Right/Left duopoly, and I don’t think that’s quite right. The interviews I’m interested in doing will include that group [of leaders].”

	“I’m not the smoothest presenter on television or reader of the autocue, but I guess they think that I manage the chaos [of live guests] well,” Phillips added. “Broadcast journalism has, to some extent, become the creature of entertainment. We need to return to the business of reporting. To put it in its crassest terms, the story needs to come before the reporter. Too many people who do what I do put themselves between the viewer and the story, and that’s not our job.”

schema.headline: CBS News Correspondent Trevor Phillips Says Editor-in-Chief Bari Weiss ‘Will Either Change the World or Crash and Burn’

title: Scott Pelley, Sharyn Alfonsi Take Journalist-in-Residence Roles at Columbia University
description:
The stopwatch keeps ticking after “60 Minutes.”

	Sharyn Alfonsi and Scott Pelley were both named journalists-in-residence at Columbia University‘s
body:
The stopwatch keeps ticking after “60 Minutes.”

	Sharyn Alfonsi and Scott Pelley were both named journalists-in-residence at Columbia University‘s School of Journalism Monday, a position that will be in place for the 2026-2027 academic term. The two former “60 Minutes” correspondents will work with students through lectures, workshops and special events, and they will each contribute a piece to the Columbia Journalism Review. 


	“We’re both excited and honored to welcome two journalists of this caliber to our Journalist in Residence Program,” said Jelani Cobb, dean of the Journalism School, in a statement. “Their distinguished track records in investigative reporting highlight the amazing opportunity our students will have to learn from them, and we look forward to having Sharyn and Scott with us this year.”
	

	Both journalists were ousted from the CBS News newsmagazine earlier this year, part of a radical overhaul of a venerable program that has continued to draw big crowds and win plaudits for its coverage. Alfonsi departed after clashing with Bari Weiss, CBS News’ editor in chief, who delayed the airing of a report the journalist had prepared investigating the deportation of migrants to harsh prisons in Venezuela. Pelley was pushed out after calling out the show’s new executive producer, Nick Bilton, during an internal meeting.

	Weiss dramatically overhauled the program in May and June, dispatching half the on-air staff and several senior producers. Tanya Simon, the former executive producer, was replaced by Bilton. In addition to Alfonsi and Pelley, Cecilia Vega was also pushed out. Anderson Cooper left earlier in the year.
	

	“Joining Columbia University as a Journalist in Residence is an extraordinary privilege, especially at a time when deep, rigorous and fearless reporting has never been more vital,” said Alfonsi, in a statement. “I’m excited to work with the next generation of journalists who are eager to ask the tough questions that hold power accountable.”

	Pelley echoed her sentiments. “This is a critical time for a free press,” he said in a statement. “Columbia is leading the way in training the next generation of great journalists and I am honored to join Sharyn in that vital cause.”

schema.headline: Scott Pelley, Sharyn Alfonsi Take Journalist-in-Residence Roles at Columbia University

title: ‘Warhammer 40,000’ Animated Series in Development at Amazon, Henry Cavill to Produce (EXCLUSIVE)
description: A “Warhammer 40,000” animated event series is in development from Amazon MGM Studios, Blur Studios, and Games Workshop, Variety has learned exclusiv
body:
A “Warhammer 40,000” animated event series is in development from Amazon MGM Studios, Blur Studios, and Games Workshop, Variety has learned exclusively. 

	In addition, Henry Cavill — who is attached to lead a live-action “Warhammer 40,000” series currently in development at Amazon — will executive produce the animated series as well. It is being developed alongside the live-action project. 


	The animated project will serve as a spinoff of the Amazon animated anthology series “Secret Level,” which featured a “Warhammer 40,000” episode when it debuted in late 2024. Blur Studios produced “Secret Level,” while Games Workshop is the manufacturer behind the tabletop miniature wargame. 
	

	Dave Wilson, who directed the “Warhammer 40,000” episode of “Secret Level” and served as the show’s supervising director, is the co-creator and director of the new animated series. He is developing it alongside John Orloff (“Masters of the Air,” “Band of Brothers”). 

	Exact plot details are under wraps, aside from the fact the series will feature The Deathwatch, an elite group of Space Marines that specialize in hunting down alien threats. 

	“Secret Level” creator Tim Miller will executive produce alongside Wilson for Blur Studios, with Cavill and Natalie Viscuso also executive producing. Roy Lee of Vertigo Entertainment executive produces with Andy Smillie from Games Workshop. The series is being developed in partnership with Amazon MGM Studios and Games Workshop

	“’Secret Level’ wasn’t conceived simply as an anthology. It was designed as a launchpad for larger stories,” said Wilson. “The response to the ‘Warhammer’ episode was extraordinary, particularly from fans who understood how much care went into getting the world right. This series gives us the opportunity to build on that foundation and tell a much larger story. I’ve wanted to tell a long-form story set in ‘Warhammer 40,000’ for more than twenty years, and I’m incredibly grateful to Games Workshop and Amazon MGM Studios for the opportunity to do it.”
	

	This is the latest announcement of an Amazon project based on game IP. In addition to “Secret Level,” Prime Video currently airs the popular series adaptation of the “Fallout” video games, while the streamer is currently prepping a “Tomb Raider” live-action show starring Sophie Turner. Amazon is also currently at work on a live-action “God of War” show, though they are on the hunt for a new lead following an on-set injury to Kratos actor Ryan Hurst. 

	A series version of “Life Is Strange” recently began production, and adaptations of games like “Mass Effect” and “Wolfenstein” are currently in development.

schema.headline: ‘Warhammer 40,000’ Animated Series in Development at Amazon, Henry Cavill to Produce (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Outplay Films Nabs Tom Tykwer-Produced Locarno Competition Title ‘I Rarely Wake Up Dreaming’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Isabelle Stever’s Locarno main competition title “I Rarely Wake Up Dreaming,” produced by Tom Tykwer, has been picked up for world sales by France’s
body:
Isabelle Stever’s Locarno main competition title “I Rarely Wake Up Dreaming,” produced by Tom Tykwer, has been picked up for world sales by France’s Outplay Films.

	Produced by Tykwer and Uwe Schott at Berlin-based X Filme Creative Pool and written by Anna Melikova, the film follows Olya and Oleh, a young queer Ukrainian couple whose love is put to the test when one partner’s gender transition collides with Russia’s full-scale invasion. As war narrows and challenges the boundaries of masculinity and femininity, they struggle to preserve their bond and sense of self.
	

	“As a Ukrainian-German filmmaking duo, we aimed to create a film that neither looks away from war nor lets it define every image,” Stever and Melikova said in a joint statement. “We place war’s violence alongside fragile quiet, fear alongside tenderness, and the extraordinary beside the everyday.


	“Inspired by our Ukrainian friends’ journey through gender transition, we explore war’s irresistible transition into everyday life,” they added. “By juxtaposing two profound transformations – one chosen, one imposed, we reflect on the topic of identity under extreme conditions. We are grateful to have found soulmates/ kindred spirits in Outplay which will gently guide the film forward with a deep understanding of its complex and sensitive themes.”

	Diego Carazo-Migerel Fougères, co-managing director and head of international sales and acquisitions at Marseille-based Outplay Films, stated: “We’re thrilled to launch this collaboration with X Filme Creative Pool on Isabel Stever’s ‘A Rarely Wake Up Dreaming.’ At a time when war casts a shadow over our history, telling the story of the invasion of Ukraine through such an original, minority-centered lens is deeply aligned with our company’s DNA. As Outplay Films continues to expand internationally, this is exactly the kind of story we want to carry as far as possible.”
	

	Expressing delight to have Outplay Films as the film’s world sales partner, Schott and Tykwer added: “Finding the right sales partner is a crucial part of a film’s journey, and in Outplay Films we have found a team whose passion for distinctive cinema and deep understanding of the film’s artistic vision make them an ideal match. We greatly value their commitment and international expertise, and we look forward to introducing ‘I Rarely Wake Up Dreaming’ to audiences around the world together.”

schema.headline: Outplay Films Nabs Tom Tykwer-Produced Locarno Competition Title ‘I Rarely Wake Up Dreaming’ (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Ben McKenzie Says Major Streamers Were Scared to License His Anti-Crypto Documentary, So He Found a Different Way to Reach Audiences
description: Ben McKenzie believes he knows why the major streaming services weren’t interested in licensing “Everyone Is Lying to You for Money.” His new docume
body:
Ben McKenzie believes he knows why the major streaming services weren’t interested in licensing “Everyone Is Lying to You for Money.” His new documentary takes on the cryptocurrency industry, portraying the controversial digital currency as corrupt and in dire need of more regulations. But the film is being released as President Donald Trump has profited handsomely from the sector, raking in $1.4 billion in combined crypto-related income during his first year back in office.
	

	“If you’re a corporation and you’re trying to decide on the marginal value of buying an independent movie that you don’t have to buy, and potentially incurring the wrath of the Trump administration, it’s a pretty easy decision,” says McKenzie. “The risk calculus is not in our favor, and they’d rather just not buy it.”


	It doesn’t matter that “Everyone Is Lying to You for Money” has received nearly universal praise (it boasts a 100% “fresh” rating on Rotten Tomatoes) since opening in April. It has also earned roughly $150,000 during its limited theatrical run, which is more than some of the films that competed for best documentary prize at last year’s Oscars. The Forge, a boutique indie studio, distributed the doc in theaters. But with its home entertainment release, McKenzie feels like major corporations are behaving as if his movie is too hot to touch.

	“I have no right to receive the money back that I’ve spent financing this movie, but it does seem wrong that certain avenues seem to be either closed or more difficult to access because of the outspokenness of my film,” McKenzie says.
	

	McKenzie could, of course, make “Everyone Is Lying to You for Money” available to rent or buy on platforms like Amazon or Apple, but that would mean forking over a percentage of the sales, as well as paying them to advertise the film on their platform. Instead, he’s cutting the major streamers out entirely and releasing the movie on Eventive, a digital platform that specializes in helping indie films reach an audience. The service doesn’t require a subscription, which McKenzie thinks could help “Everyone Is Lying to You for Money” reach an even wider audience.

	“If we can get 100,000 people in the world to watch this movie over the course of two weeks, that’ll be a phenomenal success for us,” McKenzie says. “If we can do it, then it potentially provides a way forward for other filmmakers to eventize their movies and go straight to consumers. It means you can bypass the traditional gatekeepers that are the big VOD [video-on-demand] platforms.”

	The film will be available to rent or buy on August 22. The plan is also to offer access to a live Q&A, where viewers can submit questions for McKenzie, his wife, actor Morena Baccarin, and other cryptocurrency critics and experts.

	“Hopefully they feel like they’re not just turning on Netflix or whatever and flipping through a movie, but are actually interacting with it to some degree,” McKenzie.

	McKenzie, the former star of “The O.C.” and “Gotham,” financed the production with a combination of savings and “about a million dollars” he made “betting against different frauds, crypto being sort of the primary one.” Because it was self-funded, McKenzie felt he had more freedom to speak openly about his concerns that crypto is a sham, one that fails to tell investors about the risks associated with such a volatile business.

	“I felt very strongly that the only way to make this movie correctly was to do it completely independently and to finance it myself, which I frankly have the privilege of doing because of money I’ve made in television,” McKenzie says. “I did not realize it was going to be quite this expensive or take quite this long. The old saying about independent movies is that they are never finished. You just run out of money. And that is definitely true here.”

	McKenzie first got interested in cryptocurrency during COVID lockdown when one of his friends walked him through the bitcoin economy in an effort to get him to invest. Though he had made his living as a performer, McKenzie was an economics major in college and something about the pitch didn’t sit right. So McKenzie started researching the business, growing more and more alarmed. Because crypto wasn’t heavily regulated, people could use it to launder money or pay for illegal activity, and retail investors were frequently getting fleeced, he found. Ultimately, his investigation led to the 2023 book, “Easy Money: Cryptocurrency, Casino Capitalism, and the Golden Age of Fraud,” which was written with journalist Jacob Silverman. That, in turn, led to the documentary.
	

	“You’re not afforded the protections you ought to be when you’re investing in cryptocurrency,” McKenzie says. “It’s very difficult to actually spend cryptocurrency in the real world. I can’t go to my neighborhood deli in Brooklyn and buy a bagel with Bitcoin. So it is really an investment for the retail public. You plug money into it. You hope to make money off it through no work of your own. That’s literally the definition of an investment under federal securities law. And the reason that we regulate securities differently than currencies is so people aren’t defrauded and swindled out of their money. And yet crypto has really thrived in this gray area where it’s called itself a currency and therefore has avoided a lot of the laws that would otherwise apply to it.”

	Because of his fame, McKenzie has been able to generate more attention for his crusade, appearing on cable news and writing op-eds about the dangers of cryptocurrency. 

	“I’ve gotten so many people who I think have perked up their ears a little bit and paid attention to what I’ve been doing just because it’s so unusual. ‘Oh, I didn’t know Ryan Atwood from ‘The O.C.’ had a brain,'” McKenzie says.

	McKenzie hasn’t shied away from criticizing celebrities like Kim Kardashian and Matt Damon who have made money hawking cryptocurrency companies in ads.

	“Celebrities have always shilled for products,” he says. “There’s nothing wrong with that. But these were not consumer goods. These were not soap or fast food. This was an investment vehicle. Not to presume too much, but I don’t think they know much of anything about crypto. You’re not supposed to offer people financial advice if you’re not a licensed financial adviser, and you’re specifically not supposed to sell them on what I believe cryptocurrencies to be, which are unregulated, unlicensed securities.”

	Have there been career repercussions for McKenize’s outspokenness?

	“There’s no way to quantify that,” McKenzie says. “I may not get cast in a Matt Damon movie anytime soon. That’s OK. For the record, he’s a terrific actor. He just shouldn’t have sold crypto.”

	And yes, McKenzie still plans to see “The Odyssey.”

schema.headline: Ben McKenzie Says Major Streamers Were Scared to License His Anti-Crypto Documentary, So He Found a Different Way to Reach Audiences

title: Low Light Films Boards Locarno Competition Thriller ‘O Jacaré,’ Basil Da Cunha Celebration of Lisbon’s Vibrant Reboleira District (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Deep in the mazework neighborhood of Reboleira, Lisbon, someone is hiding €180,000 ($200,000), and Portuguese-Swiss writer-director Basil Da Cunha a
body:
Deep in the mazework neighborhood of Reboleira, Lisbon, someone is hiding €180,000 ($200,000), and Portuguese-Swiss writer-director Basil Da Cunha allows the characters of “O Jacaré” to use any and all means to find it in his new feature film competing at Locarno. 

	Produced by Thera Production (Switzerland) and co-produced by Continue Walking (Portugal) and RTS Radio Télévision Suisse, “O Jacaré” wastes no time dropping its audience in the middle of a vibrant, interwoven community, using Cape Verdean music and an ensemble cast of locals to set the tension of the plot.
	

	The film, which will compete in Locarno’s main International Competition, has been boarded by Barcelona-based Low Light Films ahead of its world premiere. 


	“From the moment we saw ‘O Jacaré,’ we knew it was a film we wanted to champion,” said Jainer Morales Mena, Low Light Films founder. “We’re incredibly proud to represent it internationally and to help bring it to audiences around the world.”

	“O Jacaré” is Da Cunha’s final film set in Reboleira, as the district faces pending demolition, and he uses the feature to celebrate an era of life there. Much of the film is sun-soaked and colorful and filled with the rhythm and chaos of life in a cloistered, liminal community. Although structured around the search for the missing money, “O Jacaré” is interested in solving a mystery but all the more in observing the stylings of Reboleira itself, and it’s in this meditation on time and place that the film finds its heart.



	

					Basil Da Cunha directs ‘O Jacaré.’
									Courtesy of Low Light Films
	



	Ahead of the film’s premiere, Variety spoke with Da Cunha about returning to Locarno, as well as his bond to Reboleira. 
	

	How has your relationship with Reboleira evolved over the many years filming there, and how did that shape “O Jacaré?”

	For more than 20 years, cinema has grown alongside the people of Reboleira. It gradually stopped being something I brought into the neighborhood and became part of the neighborhood itself. Entire families have appeared in my films across generations as actors, extras, crew members or simply witnesses. We raised children together, buried friends, celebrated weddings and watched streets disappear. “O Jacaré” comes from that shared history. It isn’t just a film about Reboleira; it’s a film made from within it. As the neighborhood slowly disappears through demolition, I felt an urgency to preserve its gestures, voices, humor, music and memories before they vanished. In many ways, the film is both a celebration and an act of remembrance.

	What drew you to telling this story through such a large ensemble of characters rather than following a single protagonist?

	I’ve never experienced Reboleira as a place of individual heroes. It’s a collective world where everyone’s story constantly overlaps with everyone else’s. I wanted the film to move like the neighborhood itself: unpredictable, noisy, full of encounters and digressions. Every character carries a different generation, a different dream, a different wound. But the ensemble structure also came from another desire: “O Jacaré” is the last dance of the body of work I’ve built in Reboleira over the past 15 years. I felt an urgency to bring everyone together before this world disappeared. Some of the streets no longer exist, children have become adults, and many people have moved away. I wanted to reunite, in a single film, all the generations of people I’ve worked with throughout that journey. The film becomes both a story and a reunion: a collective portrait of a community, but also of the cinematic family we’ve built together over the years.

	Music plays a massive role in the spirit of the film. Can you talk about your process for approaching the music of the story?

	Music isn’t something I add to the film afterwards; it’s part of the life I’m filming. Most of the songs come from Cape Verdean musicians who shaped the cultural identity of the community long before I arrived. They carry memory, exile, celebration and melancholy all at once. I wanted every piece of music to feel as if it naturally belonged to the space, whether it’s heard from a passing car, a bar, a party or inside someone’s home. Rather than illustrating emotion, the music creates the emotional landscape the characters already inhabit. I also wanted the film itself to move like the music. The rhythm of the editing, the energy of the scenes and even the humor are deeply influenced by Cape Verdean funk from the 1970s. For the first time, I wanted to fully embrace the pleasure of popular genre cinema, not as an ironic reference, but as a genuine way of telling the stories of people who are rarely allowed to become larger-than-life cinematic figures. Music became the heartbeat that holds all of that together.
	

	What does it mean for “O Jacaré” to premiere in Locarno’s International Competition, especially given your long history with the festival?

	Locarno has accompanied almost my entire journey as a filmmaker. My first short film screened there in 2009, and many important moments of my career have passed through the festival since then. “O Jacaré” is now the third feature film I’ve premiered in Locarno, which makes this selection especially meaningful. It’s a recognition not only of my work, but of everyone in Reboleira who trusted cinema enough to make it part of their lives. In many ways, it feels like bringing the neighborhood onto one of the world’s biggest stages.

schema.headline: Low Light Films Boards Locarno Competition Thriller ‘O Jacaré,’ Basil Da Cunha Celebration of Lisbon’s Vibrant Reboleira District (EXCLUSIVE)

title: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Sets Imax Release as ‘The Odyssey’ Exclusive Run Ends
description:
“Spider-Man: Brand New Day” will (finally!) swing to Imax on Aug. 6. 

	Sony and Marvel’s web-slinging adventure didn’t play on the company’s premiu
body:
“Spider-Man: Brand New Day” will (finally!) swing to Imax on Aug. 6. 

	Sony and Marvel’s web-slinging adventure didn’t play on the company’s premium screens during its first few days in theaters because Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey” commanded the network’s entire domestic footprint for three weekends. Now that “The Odyssey’s” exclusive run is ending, Imax is able to schedule other blockbusters in its coveted auditoriums. 


	That being said, Nolan’s Greek epic will retain most of the company’s screens. “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” will share the Imax global network with “The Odyssey” across select digital locations. Meanwhile “The Odyssey” will continue to play across all 41 of the company’s 70mm film locations around the world. So far, “The Odyssey” has generated a staggering $221 million globally in Imax — and that’s before the blockbuster has landed in major overseas markets like China, South Korea and Japan. 
	

	Of course, “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” is already doing quite well at the box office without Imax. The superhero adventure, starring Tom Holland as Peter Parker, launched to a jaw-dropping $927 million globally, including $355 million domestically and $572 million internationally. Since “The Odyssey” has yet to premiere in certain territories in Asia, the newest Spidey adventure was able to screen in Imax across China, Japan and South Korea, delivering a combined $23 million.

	“Spider-Man has been among the most bankable superheroes at the global box office for over two decades — with the franchise delivering $365 million in Imax receipts to date — and ‘Brand New Day’ is taking that legacy to new heights with its record-breaking opening weekend,” said Rich Gelfond, CEO of Imax. “We believe more Spidey fans around the world will want to experience his latest adventure in Imax — and we hope to be a major driver of both new and repeat viewing for the latest hit in this incredible year for moviegoing.” 
	

	Thanks to the all-out frenzy around “The Odyssey,” Imax achieved its highest-grossing month in history with $257 million globally in July — 47% above its previous record. “The Odyssey,” the first feature shot entirely with Imax cameras, became the company’s fastest film to surpass $200 million. It ranks as Imax’s third-highest grossing release to date. And the benchmarks will keep coming because Imax plans to keep scheduling “The Odyssey” through at least Sept. 17.

	“We are all witness to history with ‘The Odyssey,’ which seems intent on shattering all Imax box office records in its path,” Gelfond said. “It continues to defy gravity in a way few films ever have, making it virtually impossible to predict how high it will ultimately soar.”

schema.headline: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Sets Imax Release as ‘The Odyssey’ Exclusive Run Ends

title: Modest Mouse Pulls Guitarist From Tour After Alleged DMs to Teen Surface
description:
Modest Mouse Guitarist
                          Booted From Tour Over Alleged DMs to Teen
body:
Modest Mouse Guitarist
                          Booted From Tour Over Alleged DMs to Teen
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              
                August 2, 2026
                
                            3:30 PM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  August 2, 2026
                                4:48 PM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Modest Mouse guitarist Simon O'Connor is sitting out the band's next tour after allegedly sliding into an underage fan's DMs with an explicit image ... then telling her a night of partying -- and her bikini pics -- helped spark the exchange.
      
    
            The fan shared screenshots on Reddit showing messages O'Connor allegedly sent before her 17th birthday. She claims her age was clearly displayed on her Instagram bio at the time.
      
    
      
        
              
    
    
            Take a look through the DMs ... the alleged exchange starts with O'Connor sending a meme and a sexually explicit image, prompting the teen to ask whether he'd been hacked.
      

            O'Connor allegedly said he hadn't been hacked and blamed the messages on a "party night" ... before suggesting the fan's bikini photos had also caught his attention.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The guitarist -- who joined the band in 2021 and played on their latest album, "An Eraser and a Maze"-- later posted his own lengthy explanation on the Modest Mouse subreddit ... saying he mistook the teen for someone who had repeatedly harassed and pranked him through fake accounts.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            O'Connor admitted he used "poor judgement" when he fired off what he called a tasteless meme and a "Simon calls your bluff" sticker ... but said he unsent the messages and ended the conversation once he realized he had the wrong person.
      
    
            He apologized to the fan ... saying she didn't deserve to be put in that position, and said he strongly opposes any sexual behavior involving minors.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Modest Mouse has since announced O'Connor won't join its upcoming North American tour, which kicks off Tuesday in Ojai, California ... Seth Jabour of Les Savy Fav will step in on guitar in his place.
      
    
            The band didn't clarify whether O'Connor is gone for good ... but for now, he's definitely not floating on with the tour.
      
    
            We've reached out to the band's reps ... so far, no word back.

title: Ariana Grande Pulls Out of London Stage Revival with Jonathan Bailey Amid Public Scrutiny
description:
Ariana Grande
                          Drops Out of Show with Jonathan Bailey ...
body:
Ariana Grande
                          Drops Out of Show with Jonathan Bailey ...
                          Amid Public Criticism
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              
                August 2, 2026
                
                            4:30 PM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  August 3, 2026
                                6:28 AM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Ariana Grande isn't just stepping away from the spotlight following her "Eternal Sunshine Tour," she's hitting pause on her acting career and chance to reunite with former co-star Jonathan Bailey.
      
    
            The pop superstar has officially withdrawn from the upcoming London revival of Stephen Sondheim's "Sunday in the Park With George," where she had been set to work again with her 'Wicked' co-star at the Barbican in 2027.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Grande's rep said in a statement to PEOPLE the decision is part of a broader plan to take a break from public-facing work once she wraps up her massively successful "Eternal Sunshine Tour" and intends to "take a step back from visibility" after the tour concludes
      

            According to the rep, Grande wants to finish the run "on a high note, both healthily and happily," before taking what her team describes as a "much-deserved break."
      
    
            The statement also points to the downside of fame, saying public appearances have subjected Grande to "endless, ongoing public scrutiny." Her rep added that Ariana has loved every minute of performing for fans during the tour and is grateful for the experience, but now feels it's time to prioritize herself.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            That means "Sunday in the Park With George" is officially off her calendar. The show's official account confirmed the acclaimed musical will still move forward as planned despite Grande's exit. Her role will be recast before the show opens at London's Barbican.
      
    
            The revival had generated major buzz thanks to the planned reunion of Grande and Bailey following their performances in 'Wicked,' making her departure a significant shake-up for theater fans.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            As for Ariana, it sounds like the next chapter won't involve red carpets, premieres or Broadway stages ... at least not for a while. After years of nonstop music, movies and public attention, she's choosing to step out of the spotlight and recharge.
